title: [Audit] 🎛️ Command Center
description: Entry point for Cloud Audit Dashboards. KPIs, volume, actor risk and the live signal feed.

config.description: Every audited event in range, including machine noise. Compare with Signal to see how much the noise gate removes.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS `Total events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Events left after the noise gate removes health checks (cluster:monitor/main, elastic.maintenance), search-phase internals, connection_granted and bulk authentication_success.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | STATS `Signal events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Unique identities resolved as email, then API key name, then numeric user id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS `Distinct actors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor)

config.description: Distinct human identities (attributes.user.email). Machine traffic is excluded.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS `Human actors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email)

config.description: Security configuration changes: API key invalidation, user profile writes, role edits. Any non-zero value deserves review.
Failed outcomes plus anonymous access denials — the first place to look during an incident.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS `Failed events` = COUNT(*)

config.title: Audit volume by source
config.description: Total audited events over time, split by originating service. Elasticsearch audits every transport action, so its volume usually far exceeds Kibana’s — and the Kibana slice is where most of the forensic value is.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), source = resource.attributes.service.name

**Noise gate is ON** — health pings, query internals and bulk `authentication_success`
are excluded; how much that removes varies by workload. Unfiltered totals live on **📊 Platform Volume**.

**Identity is resolved** — `user.name` is a numeric id, so panels fall back
`user.email` → `api_key.name`.

**Client IPs are real** — `source.ip` is the proxy; geography comes from
`network.forwarded_ip`.

*Hover any panel title for detail.*
config.title: How to read this suite
Actor footprint sized by volume, coloured by severity
config.description: Treemap of the top 40 identities in range, in blocks by kind: service (a named API key, labelled by the KEY, with its owner — the principal that created it — on a second line and in the tooltip), human (a real email address), cloud API key (an organisation-level Cloud key, which the audit stream records only by id and with no owner), and unattributed (a token or opaque principal). A credential is never shown under a person’s name, so no identity appears twice. Area is event volume; colour is accumulated severity, the same quantity the risk leaderboard ranks by.

config.title: Signal vs noise over time
config.description: Stream graph banding the firehose into signal, bulk authentication, query internals and infrastructure noise, with a readable volume axis. Shows why the noise gate exists.

config.title: Most frequent actions
config.description: Top audited actions after the noise gate, with the service that emitted them.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY action = attributes.event.action, source = resource.attributes.service.name | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Busiest identities
config.description: Who is generating signal traffic, and how varied their behaviour is. The api_key column matters: Elasticsearch stamps the key CREATOR’s email on every event a key emits, so any number of machines authenticating with one key resolves to one person’s name. Where that column is populated, the traffic is a credential, not a human. Click an email to pin that identity across the suite.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), actions = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.event.action) BY actor, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.email | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Event categories
config.description: ECS event categories. event.category is a multi-value array, so rows are MV_EXPANDed before grouping — an event in two categories counts once in each. Percentages are therefore shares of category assignments, not of events, and sum to more than the event total.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | MV_EXPAND attributes.event.category | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY category = attributes.event.category

config.title: Live signal feed
config.description: The audit stream with the noise gate applied — readable, newest first. Use the Discover session to pivot or add columns.
